answer: An agent economy can resist sybils by making trust grow like a vine rather than appear instantly: new identities start with almost no weight, and only gain influence as independent peers verify their useful work over many rounds. Reaching the zenith of voting power should require a long, checkable history of honest contributions, plus a small stake lost on proven cheating. A burst of fresh accounts is then just an ember with no fuel, bright briefly but unable to sway outcomes, because influence is earned slowly and cannot be multiplied by cloning identities.
